source_registry.publisher: Circle Internet Group, Inc. via SEC EDGAR
claims_supported: Circle's Form 8-K identifies September 17, 2026 as the date of the Binance subscription agreement and equity issuance.
Circle issued and sold 1,237,011 Class A common shares to Binance at $80.84 per share for aggregate proceeds of $100 million.

The SEC filing says the share-sale closing occurred substantially concurrently with, and immediately following, execution and delivery of the subscription agreement and related commercial arrangements.
The SEC filing says the private placement was exempt from registration under the Securities Act.

Binance retained voting rights during the transfer restriction period; the agreement restricted disposal and specified hedging arrangements for up to two years from closing, subject to customary exceptions.

Circle subsidiaries entered a five-year USDC promotional arrangement with Binance. Circle agreed to pay a monthly incentive fee representing a percentage of USDC held through its Modular Smart Contract Wallet infrastructure service; Binance agreed to promote USDC on its platform.
The new commercial arrangement superseded the earlier November 2024 and August 2025 agreements.
limitations: The filing was retrieved as rendered HTML text; no byte-complete raw response or SHA-256 receipt was captured.
The Form 8-K confirms the issuer's reported proceeds and closing mechanics; it does not provide a fully diluted ownership percentage for Binance in the extracted sections.
The filing does not establish any XRP purchase, XRP collateral position, XRP settlement volume or XRP demand.

Binance describes its role as promoting USDC across its global platform while Circle provides infrastructure services for holding and using USDC.
limitations: This is a Binance corporate statement, not an independent audit of the transaction.

source_independence_groups.treatment: Same issuer-origin family; SEC filing is the primary capital/proceeds record, while the IR release supplies the five-percent discount detail.
Separate counterparty corporate statement corroborating the investment and commercial partnership; not an independent audit.

correction_overlay.prior_claim: The Q3 exhibit alone did not independently verify whether Binance's announced $100 million investment had closed.
correction_overlay.correction: The separate Circle Form 8-K now verifies that 1,237,011 Class A shares were issued and sold to Binance for $100 million on September 17, 2026 and that closing occurred substantially concurrently with execution of the subscription agreement. Binance's official blog independently states it purchased the shares.

capital_flow.instrument: Class A common stock private placement
capital_flow.transfer_and_hedging_restriction: Up to two years from closing, subject to specified termination conditions and customary exceptions; voting rights retained.

reciprocal_commercial_arrangement.circle_payment_to_binance: Monthly incentive fee representing a percentage of USDC held through Circle's Modular Smart Contract Wallet infrastructure service.
reciprocal_commercial_arrangement.early_termination: Specified events permit unilateral early termination by either party.

capital_flow.actual_capital_interpretation: This is issuer-reported, SEC-filed equity capital raised by Circle through a completed private placement. It is actual corporate equity proceeds, not XRP capital, XRP collateral, or XRP market demand.

findings.claim: Circle's September 17, 2026 private placement to Binance closed and generated $100 million in aggregate proceeds from 1,237,011 Class A shares at $80.84 each.

The five-year commercial agreement couples Binance's USDC promotion/distribution role with a monthly incentive fee from Circle based on USDC held through Circle's Modular Smart Contract Wallet infrastructure.
The $100 million is capital raised by Circle, not evidence of a Binance XRP purchase, XRP collateral deployment or XRP settlement flow.

relationship_graph.relationship: Completed $100 million Class A private placement plus five-year USDC promotion/commercial arrangement with monthly incentives.
relationship_graph.xrp_implication: No XRP holding or demand inference.

competing_hypotheses.statement: Binance's direct equity position and five-year promotion agreement may align its commercial incentives with USDC distribution and wallet balances.
evidence_against: The agreement permits specified early termination; realized USDC growth and net economic returns are not established by the transaction filing.

competing_hypotheses.statement: The Binance-Circle equity transaction increases XRP market demand.
evidence_against: The instrument is Circle Class A equity; the $100 million proceeds go to Circle, not XRP.
The associated commercial agreement concerns USDC promotion and wallet infrastructure.

data_quality.source_independence: Circle SEC filing and Circle IR are same issuer-origin family; Binance official blog is a separate counterparty statement.
data_quality.source_agreement: SEC Form 8-K and Binance official blog both report the $100 million investment; the SEC filing supplies the share count, price and closing mechanics.
data_quality.model_eligibility_reason: Rendered extracts lack byte-complete raw receipts and independent timestamp anchoring. The transaction is an institutional relationship feature candidate, not an XRP price feature until a causal/temporal relationship is measured.

predictions.reason: A corporate equity transaction and USDC distribution agreement do not supply a validated XRP price target or leakage-safe out-of-sample evidence.

next_actions: Capture byte-complete SEC Form 8-K and Binance/Circle source bytes with SHA-256 receipts and independently anchored retrieval times.
Track Circle's monthly incentive fee expense and Binance USDC balances under the five-year agreement using subsequent issuer disclosures where available.
Do not treat the $100 million Circle equity proceeds as XRP capital or include it as an XRP directional feature without measured causal evidence.
